topic.title: Spatial Reasoning and Grounded Scene Representations
topic.overview: Spatial understanding requires more than recognizing the objects in an image. Models must recover locations, perspectives, distances, and relationships, then connect those quantities to language or action. This cluster combines explicit scene geometry, structured latent representations, and evaluation tasks designed to distinguish spatial reasoning from semantic shortcuts.
topic.whyItMatters: An instruction such as selecting the object behind another object depends on geometry rather than object names alone. Better representations and benchmarks can support grounded interaction, but success on a specialized localization task should not be equated with general three-dimensional reasoning.
topic.evolution: A 2010 representative introduces volumetric constraints for reasoning jointly about room layout and objects. Recent work emphasizes vision-language grounding and deliberately difficult spatial queries: Surprise3D removes object names from human-annotated queries to reduce shortcuts. In 2026, WorldComp2D studies efficient representations of identity and proximity, using facial landmark localization as its proof of concept.
openQuestions: How can benchmarks separate genuine spatial reasoning from learned scene conventions?
Which spatial representations transfer across cameras, environments, and instruction styles?

papers.title: SceneForge: Enhancing 3D-text alignment with Structured Scene Compositions
